title: Meet JavaScript
objective: Print with console.log, write comments and read error messages
story: Welcome to Launch Base, captain! Your rocket is on the launch pad, but the control panel is waiting for your commands. The rocket speaks **JavaScript**: today you'll send it your first message.

sections.title: What is JavaScript?
sections.body:
JavaScript is the programming language that brings web pages to life. The menu that opens when you press a button, the score in a game, your position on a map: JavaScript is behind most of them.

JavaScript runs inside the browser, so you don't need to install anything special: your browser already understands it.

sections.title: Talking with console.log
Comments
An error message is a clue
sections.body:
If something is wrong in your code, you'll see a red error message. Don't worry: the message tells you **where** and **what** went wrong.

```js
consle.log("Hello");
```

This code gives the error `consle is not defined`: `console` is misspelled. Look at the line number in the message, read that line carefully, fix it and run it again. Programmers spend a big part of their day doing exactly this.

examples.title: First signal
examples.note: Run the code and look at the output in the Console.

examples.title: Numbers and text
examples.note: 3 + 4 inside quotes isn't calculated; it's printed as it is.

tasks.title: First signal
tasks.prompt: Send exactly this message to mission control: `Hello, space!`
tasks.solution:
// Write your message below
console.log("Hello, space!");
hints: The text must be in quotes: "Hello, space!"

tasks.title: Launch checklist
tasks.prompt:
Before launch, print the checklist in order. Each line should be a separate `console.log`:

```
Fuel: ok
Engine: ok
Ready for launch!
```
tasks.starter:
console.log("Fuel: ok");

// Add the other two lines
hints: Write a separate console.log for each line.
Order matters: first Engine, then Ready for launch!

tasks.title: Flight math
tasks.prompt: How many hours are there in a year? Don't calculate it yourself: let JavaScript do **`365 * 24`** inside `console.log`.
hints: The multiplication sign is the * (star) character.
If you put the calculation in quotes, it won't be calculated!

challenge.title: Countdown in one line
challenge.prompt:
Print these 4 lines using a single `console.log`:

```
3
2
1
Ignition!
```

Hint: `\n` inside text starts a new line.
hints: When "a\nb" is printed, a and b land on separate lines.

project_task.title: Title screen
project_task.prompt:
Let's print the title screen of our game **Star Hunter**. Print these three lines; on the second line, put your own name or nickname after `Pilot:`:

```
*** STAR HUNTER ***
Pilot: Alex
Mission: collect 10 stars!
```
hints: You can write three separate console.log lines.
The second line must start with "Pilot: " followed by your name.
